name: UPSC CSE 2028
subtitle: Optional: Anthropology (Papers I and II)
notes: The 2028 UPSC calendar is not out yet (expected around May 2027). Prelims and Mains dates are tentative, following the 2027 pattern (Prelims 23 May 2027, Mains from 20 Aug 2027). Edit them when the calendar is published.

GS-IV mixes theory questions and case studies, so its question count is left blank. Optional papers: answer 5 of 8 questions (Q1 and Q5 compulsory), 50 marks each. The two language papers are qualifying only and do not count towards rank.

syllabus.title: GS-I: Heritage, History, Geography and Society
syllabus.description: Mains GS Paper I; also covers the history, culture and geography parts of Prelims GS-I.

syllabus.title: Indian art and culture
syllabus.description: Salient aspects of art forms, literature and architecture from ancient to modern times.

syllabus.title: History
syllabus.description: Indian history from ancient times to post-independence, and world history.

syllabus.title: Ancient India
syllabus.description: Prehistory to early medieval India: Harappan and Vedic cultures, religions, empires and dynasties.

syllabus.title: Medieval India
syllabus.description: Early medieval kingdoms, the Delhi Sultanate, Mughals, regional states and Bhakti-Sufi movements.

syllabus.title: Modern India and the freedom struggle
syllabus.description: Mid-eighteenth century to 1947: colonial rule, reform movements and the stages of the freedom struggle.

syllabus.title: Post-independence consolidation
syllabus.description: Consolidation and reorganisation within the country after independence.

syllabus.title: World history
syllabus.description: Events from the eighteenth century: industrial revolution, world wars, redrawal of boundaries, political philosophies.

syllabus.title: Indian society
syllabus.description: Salient features of Indian society, role of women, population, poverty, urbanisation and social empowerment.

syllabus.title: Geography
syllabus.description: Physical, Indian and world geography for Prelims and Mains.

syllabus.title: Physical geography
syllabus.description: Landforms, climate, oceans and geophysical phenomena, with changes in critical features.

syllabus.title: Indian geography
syllabus.description: Physiography, drainage, climate, resources and location of industries in India.

syllabus.title: World geography and resources
syllabus.description: Distribution of key natural resources across the world, including South Asia and the Indian subcontinent.

syllabus.title: GS-II: Polity, Governance, Social Justice and IR
syllabus.description: Mains GS Paper II; also covers the polity and governance parts of Prelims GS-I.

syllabus.title: Indian Polity and Constitution
syllabus.description: Constitution, its evolution and basic structure, Union and State institutions, and constitutional bodies.

syllabus.title: Governance
syllabus.description: Government policies, transparency and accountability, e-governance, civil services and development actors.

syllabus.title: Social justice
syllabus.description: Welfare schemes for vulnerable sections, and issues of health, education and human resources.

syllabus.title: International relations
syllabus.description: India and its neighbourhood, bilateral and global groupings, and important international institutions.

syllabus.title: GS-III: Economy, Environment, S&T, Security and Disasters
syllabus.description: Mains GS Paper III; also covers the economy, environment and science parts of Prelims GS-I.

syllabus.title: Indian economy
syllabus.description: Growth, planning, resource mobilisation, inclusive growth, budgeting, banking and infrastructure.

syllabus.title: Agriculture and food
syllabus.description: Cropping patterns, irrigation, farm subsidies and MSP, PDS, food processing and land reforms.

syllabus.title: Science and technology
syllabus.description: Developments in science and technology, indigenisation, and the General Science part of Prelims.

syllabus.title: Environment and ecology
syllabus.description: Conservation, pollution, environmental impact assessment, biodiversity and climate change.

syllabus.title: Internal security
syllabus.description: Internal security challenges, cyber security, border management and the security forces.

syllabus.title: Disaster management
syllabus.description: Types of disasters, preparedness, mitigation and the disaster management framework.

syllabus.title: GS-IV: Ethics, Integrity and Aptitude
syllabus.description: Mains GS Paper IV: ethics theory and case studies.

syllabus.title: Ethics: concepts and thinkers
syllabus.description: Ethics and human interface, attitude, aptitude for civil service, emotional intelligence, thinkers and probity in governance.

syllabus.title: Ethics case studies
syllabus.description: Case studies on the topics of the GS-IV syllabus.

syllabus.title: Essay
syllabus.description: Mains Essay paper: two essays, one from each section.

syllabus.title: CSAT (Prelims Paper II)
syllabus.description: Prelims General Studies Paper II, qualifying at 33%.

syllabus.title: Comprehension
syllabus.description: Reading comprehension passages and inference questions.

syllabus.title: Logical reasoning and analytical ability
syllabus.description: Logical reasoning and analytical ability.

syllabus.title: General mental ability
syllabus.description: General mental ability.

syllabus.title: Basic numeracy and data interpretation
syllabus.description: Basic numeracy (numbers and their relations, orders of magnitude) and data interpretation at Class X level.

syllabus.title: Decision making and interpersonal skills
syllabus.description: Decision making, problem solving, and interpersonal and communication skills.

syllabus.title: Optional: Anthropology Paper I
syllabus.description: Anthropology Paper I: foundations, biological anthropology, prehistory and socio-cultural anthropology.

syllabus.title: Meaning, scope and branches of anthropology
syllabus.description: Meaning, scope and development of anthropology; its relationship with other disciplines; and its main branches.

syllabus.title: Human evolution and theories of evolution
syllabus.description: Biological and cultural factors in human evolution; pre-Darwinian, Darwinian and post-Darwinian theories; terms of evolutionary biology.

syllabus.title: Primates
syllabus.description: Characteristics of primates, evolutionary trends and taxonomy, primate adaptations and behaviour.

syllabus.title: Fossil hominids
syllabus.description: Phylogenetic status, characteristics and distribution of Plio-Pleistocene hominids, Homo erectus, Neanderthals and Homo sapiens.

syllabus.title: Biological basis of life
syllabus.description: The cell, DNA structure and replication, protein synthesis, gene, mutation, chromosomes and cell division.

syllabus.title: Prehistoric archaeology
syllabus.description: Principles of prehistoric archaeology, relative and absolute dating, and the broad outline of prehistoric cultures.

syllabus.title: Nature of culture and society
syllabus.description: The concept and characteristics of culture and society, and related concepts.

syllabus.title: Marriage, family and kinship
syllabus.description: Definitions, forms and functions of marriage and family, and kinship terminology, descent and alliance.

syllabus.title: Economic organisation
syllabus.description: Meaning, scope and relevance of economic anthropology; production, distribution and exchange in tribal and peasant societies.

syllabus.title: Political organisation and social control
syllabus.description: Band, tribe, chiefdom, kingdom and state; power and authority; social control, law and justice in simple societies.

syllabus.title: Religion
syllabus.description: Anthropological approaches to religion; magic, religion and science; specialists and witchcraft.

syllabus.title: Anthropological theories
syllabus.description: Classical and later theories from evolutionism and diffusionism to functionalism, structuralism and postmodernism.

syllabus.title: Culture, language and communication
syllabus.description: Nature, origin and characteristics of language; verbal and non-verbal communication; language in social context.

syllabus.title: Research methods in anthropology
syllabus.description: Fieldwork tradition, techniques, methods and methodology of data collection and analysis.

syllabus.title: Human genetics
syllabus.description: Methods and applications of human genetics, Mendelian and population genetics, and chromosomal aberrations.

syllabus.title: Race, racism and genetic markers
syllabus.description: Race and racism, biological basis of variation, and age, sex and population variation as genetic markers.

syllabus.title: Ecological and epidemiological anthropology
syllabus.description: Biological adaptation and acclimatisation, and the epidemiology of infectious and non-infectious diseases.

syllabus.title: Human growth and development
syllabus.description: Concept, stages and factors of human growth and development, and methods of studying them.

syllabus.title: Fertility and demographic anthropology
syllabus.description: Bio-events and fertility, demographic theories, and factors influencing fecundity, fertility, natality and mortality.

syllabus.title: Applications of anthropology
syllabus.description: Anthropology of sports, nutrition, defence and designing, forensic anthropology, and applied human genetics.

syllabus.title: Optional: Anthropology Paper II
syllabus.description: Anthropology Paper II: Indian culture and society, tribes, and anthropology in India.

syllabus.title: Evolution of Indian culture and civilisation
syllabus.description: Prehistoric and protohistoric India, palaeo-anthropological evidence from India, and ethno-archaeology.

syllabus.title: Demographic profile of India
syllabus.description: Ethnic and linguistic elements in the Indian population, its distribution and factors of growth.

syllabus.title: Traditional Indian social system and caste
syllabus.description: Structure of the traditional Indian social system, and theories, features and change in the caste system.

syllabus.title: Sacred complex and religions in Indian society
syllabus.description: The sacred complex and nature-man-spirit complex, and the impact of religions on Indian society.

syllabus.title: Anthropology in India
syllabus.description: Emergence and growth of anthropology in India and contributions of Indian anthropologists.

syllabus.title: Indian village, minorities and social change
syllabus.description: The Indian village, linguistic and religious minorities, and processes of socio-cultural change.

syllabus.title: Tribal situation and problems
syllabus.description: Tribal situation in India, problems of tribal communities, and the impact of development projects and displacement.

syllabus.title: SC, ST and OBC: deprivation, safeguards and ethnicity
syllabus.description: Exploitation and deprivation of SC, ST and OBC, constitutional safeguards, social change and ethnicity.

syllabus.title: Religions, tribes and the nation state
syllabus.description: Impact of religions on tribal societies, and the tribe in relation to the nation state.

syllabus.title: Tribal administration and development
syllabus.description: History of tribal administration and policies, development programmes, and the role of anthropology in development.
